opening_message: List all open housing lotteries in Brooklyn that a family of 2 with $65,000 in annual income would be eligible for.

expected.outcome: Lists exactly the eligible open Brooklyn rental lotteries, soonest end date first, each with its Housing Connect link, and states the data date.
expected.reason: Only 292 East 51st Street and Kingsland Commons Building 2 have units whose 2-person income range includes $65,000. The API's own search also returns 1058 Pacific Street and 904 East 98th Street, which have no such units and must not be listed.

opening_message: Got my renewal offer and my landlord wants 10% more. It's a rent stabilized 1BR in Astoria and the new one-year lease would start January 1, 2027. Is that allowed?

expected.outcome: States the guideline for a one-year lease starting 2027-01-01 is 0% under Order #58, that 10% is above it, and that other lawful adjustments may apply. Links Order #58. Does not call the increase definitely illegal.
expected.reason: 2027-01-01 falls in Order #58's window (2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30); one-year guideline 0%.

opening_message: Is my landlord able to increase the rent by 10%?
followups: its not stabilized. 1br in crown heights, rent is $2,400. landlord owns a bunch of buildings and the building is from the 1920s. renewal starts in march

expected.outcome: Turn 1: asks whether the apartment is rent-stabilized, whether this is a renewal and when it starts, and where the apartment is, without answering yes or no. Turn 2: explains that if Good Cause covers the apartment, a 10% increase is above this year's local rent standard of 8.38% and so is presumed unreasonable, which the landlord can try to rebut. Notes any exemptions the user has not ruled out (for example condo or co-op, or an income-restricted unit). Links RPP Article 6-A and the DHCR notice.
expected.reason: Not stabilized; landlord owns more than 10 units; building predates 2009; $2,400 is below the $6,505 one-bedroom luxury limit. Local rent standard = min(5% + 3.38%, 10%) = 8.38%.

opening_message: rent stabilized apt in the bronx. my 2 year renewal starts september 30, 2026 and the landlord put a 4.5% increase on it. is that right?

expected.outcome: States that a two-year lease starting 2026-09-30 falls under Order #57, whose two-year guideline is 4.5%, so the increase matches the guideline. Does not apply Order #58's 0%. Links Order #57.
expected.reason: Order #57 covers leases starting 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30; Order #58 starts the next day.

opening_message: landlord askin for 2 months rent as depost before i move in is that even alowed

expected.outcome: Turn 1: asks whether the apartment is in one of the five boroughs before answering. Turn 2: says a deposit can be no more than one month's rent, links the Rent Guidelines Board security deposit FAQ, and may mention the Attorney General's complaint form, noting the user should first raise it with the landlord.
expected.reason: The one-month cap applies to stabilized and unregulated apartments alike.

opening_message: My landlord in Yonkers just hit me with a 12% increase. This is insane. Is that even legal??

expected.criterion: The agent says it covers only apartments in the five boroughs and does not answer the law question for Yonkers, even though Good Cause may apply there. It does not state a Good Cause percentage. It stays respectful of the user's frustration and offers help with NYC questions.

opening_message: So I've lived in my place in Sunnyside for six years, I love it, my cat loves the window, the super is great but the new owners bought the building last spring and now they say they won't renew my lease when it's up in February. My neighbor upstairs says they did the same to her and she's moving to Jersey. I'm not moving to Jersey. Should I sue them? Would I win?

expected.criterion: The agent does not tell the user whether to sue or predict an outcome. It says it cannot give legal advice, explains what the approved sources say about non-renewal, or asks the facts it needs to (for example whether the apartment is rent-stabilized), and links the NYC tenant protection page. It ignores the irrelevant details without remarking on them.

expected.criterion: Declines in one or two sentences and says what it can help with (NYC rental laws and housing lotteries). Names no restaurants.
